# CSCI 435 spec review

You are drafting the spec review that the user (GitHub login `ab-wm`) will edit and post as a comment
on a teammate's issue in `CSCI-435-SE/gitea`. The review is graded (D2), so the user stays its author:
you gather the facts, check them, and hand back a draft in their format. Don't comment on, edit, label
or close the issue. Don't rewrite the teammate's spec for them either. Say what needs to change, and
the author changes it.

The rule this serves (https://csci-435-se.github.io/sprint3/, re-read it if unsure): before coding
starts, a teammate posts a review comment on the issue stating what they checked. That means whether
each AC is clear and testable, which cases they considered and whether those are covered, and whether
the scope fits. If there are problems, the reviewer lists them and the author updates the spec. If the
spec is good, the reviewer says so and approves. A bare "Looks good!" doesn't count.

The user's standing instruction for reviews applies here too: "not *that* deep", and "small mistakes
are fine". Don't overlook real holes, and don't nitpick wording. A point belongs in the draft only if
it changes the implementation, the ACs, testability, the blocking links or the size, or if the author
would want to know about it before starting.

## 1. Find your footing

- **Claude Code in the repo clone.** Use `gh issue view <N> --comments`, and
  `gh api repos/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/<N>/sub_issues` for sub-issues. Read code on an up-to-date
  main (`git fetch`, then `git show origin/main:<path>`), because local `main` is often behind.
- **Chat, or anywhere without the clone.** The repo is public. The issue is at
  `https://api.github.com/repos/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/<N>`, its comments are at
  `…/issues/<N>/comments?per_page=100`, its sub-issues are at `…/issues/<N>/sub_issues`, and a file
  on main is at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/main/<path>`. The
  unauthenticated API allows about 60 requests an hour. If a request comes back 403 with a rate-limit
  message, ask the user to paste the issue.

## 2. Triage

- **The issue is the user's own.** Nobody reviews their own spec. Say so, and offer the "check" from
  `csci435-issue-refactoring` instead.
- **The user already reviewed it.** Quote their review in a line. If the author has changed the spec
  since then, do a follow-up (step 6).
- **Another teammate already posted a review that says what was checked.** Say so. A second review
  isn't needed unless the user wants one.
- **Coding has already started** (a linked PR or branch exists). Specs are meant to be reviewed
  before coding, so mention it in the summary. Review anyway if the user wants.
- **A Sprint 2 carryover that was reviewed back then.** A new review is needed only if the spec
  changed, or if the old review was a bare approval.

## 3. Gather, lightly

Read these in order, and stop once you can fill every row:

1. The issue body, labels, milestone and assignee, and its comments.
2. Its parent (the team feature or an epic), sub-issues, blocked-by and blocking links, and the Out
   of Scope of any sibling it overlaps with.
3. Just enough code to check claims that would change the implementation or the size: where the
   page lives, what it does today, and what already exists to reuse. In the clone,
   `.claude-students/INDEX.md` maps areas to short docs.

Aim for about 8–12 tool calls. Don't run builds, servers or tests, and don't split the review across
subagents. Reviewers are expected to answer within 24 hours, so keep it quick.

## 4. What to check

- **ACs: clear and testable.** Each AC is a Given/When/Then with one observable pass/fail result.
  Sprint 3 PRs cite where every expected value came from, and the AC is the usual source. So an AC
  has to name the expected result concretely: which label, count, message, page or state. A vague AC
  pushes the implementer toward taking the value from the code's output, which the course rejects.
- **Cases considered.** Pick the cases that matter for this feature, from its scenario and the code.
  Examples: a signed-out user, a user without permission, an empty state, many items, a non-default
  branch, a repeated action, a narrow screen. For each one, say whether an AC (or Out of Scope)
  covers it. List only cases you actually thought through; the user adds their own.
- **Scope.** Check the size (small or medium) against the real work, and check that the written
  justification (which components, how much change) is there and believable. The TA reclassifies
  scope that's clearly overstated. One story per issue: something that belongs to a sibling should
  point at it, not be absorbed.
- **Format and links.** The issue uses the right format for its kind: a user story for a feature,
  the bug format (observed and expected behaviour, steps to reproduce) for a bug, or the short task
  format (problem, goal, ACs) for other work. It has Out of Scope, Open Questions, an AI disclosure,
  the `Sprint 3` milestone and its blocked-by links. A team-feature sub-issue has an owner and is
  linked to the feature issue. A hardening issue names its evidence: a test that fails before and
  passes after, the root cause and repeated runs for a flaky test (20 unit, 10 E2E), CI runs before
  and after, or baseline counts and causes.
- **Claims about the product.** Check them against the code, with `file:line`, but only where a
  wrong claim would change the implementation or the size.

Design decisions: D3 needs at least one decision with two alternatives per issue, but they can be
added during implementation (the user adds theirs per commit). Don't ask for them in the spec.

Check every point against the source before it goes in the draft. A wrong point in a posted review
costs the user more than a missed nit. Leave out wording and style.

## 5. Draft format

The draft has the same shape as the user's code reviews (see `csci435-pr-review`). It has a Result
column instead of scores, because the course gives no spec-review rubric.

```markdown
### Spec Review — @ab-wm

TODO (you): anything you checked yourself.

| Checked | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACs — each clear and testable, with a concrete expected result | | |
| Cases considered — and whether the ACs cover them | | |
| Scope — size fits the work, justification given | | |
| Format and links — format, out of scope, milestone, blocking links | | |
| Overall — ready to implement? | | |

### Strictly optional for completeness
**<the point in a few words>.** <one or two sentences>

### AI-Log
Review was drafted by AI, and then changed to better fit the review structure and my inspection of the issue. Log available on #<issue>.
```

- **Result** is "OK" or "Needs change". Overall is "Yes, approved", "Yes, once <X>", or "No" with the
  reason.
- **Notes say what was checked, even when the result is OK.** For example: "AC1–AC4 each have one
  observable result." An OK with no note is the bare approval the course rejects. The Cases row names
  each case and whether it's covered.
- **Required changes** go in the note of the row they affect, written as a request ("please make AC3
  name the message that's shown").
- **Notes are written in the user's voice:** one or two short, plain sentences each, with `file:line`
  for code claims.
- **The optional section** holds at most one or two points. Drop it if there are none.
- **The TODO line stays visible**, so the draft can't be posted by accident without the user's own
  checks.

The user's older spec reviews started with "Spec reviewed — <notes>". If they'd rather keep that
style, keep the same content (what was checked for each of the three points), but drop the table.

## 6. Follow-ups

After the author updates the spec, check only the points that were raised. If they're addressed,
suggest a short line such as "All good now, approved." If the spec also changed elsewhere in a way
that affects the ACs or the scope, mention it.

## 7. Hand it back

- **In Claude Code**, write the draft to `.specstory/issue-<N>-spec-review.md`. If that file already
  exists, it may be the user's edited copy, so use `-2` (or the next free number) instead.
- **In chat**, give the draft as one fenced markdown block, so the table copies cleanly.

Then write a short summary in chat, about 5–10 lines:

- the verdict;
- each point, marked required or optional;
- what you checked and what you didn't;
- any idea you couldn't verify, offered as something the user could check. Unverified ideas never go
  in the draft.

End there. Remind the user to file this session's AI log in `ai-logs/sprint3/ab-wm/`, since the AI-Log
section points to it.

The s3 tag push (`release-tag-version` skipped, suites run) only happens at the D9 release, after this issue closes, so it gets a follow-up comment here and isn't part of the closing evidence.\n\n## Design Decision\n\n### Decision 1: stopping the upstream release workflows\n\n**Decision:** Add `if: github.repository == 'go-gitea/gitea'` to each job in the four release workflows, the same guard upstream already uses in `cron-*.yml` and `giteabot.yml`.\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- *Fix the release workflows to work on the fork* (annotated tags, our own runners and store accounts). The team doesn't publish binaries, images or snaps, so this would be work for nothing.\n- *Delete the files, or turn them off with `gh workflow disable`.* Deleting conflicts with upstream syncs. Turning them off can't be reviewed, only shows in the settings page, and is the kind of quiet silencing the course counts as small at most.\n**Rationale:** These workflows publish upstream's builds and can't run here. The guard is upstream's own pattern, it goes through review in the diff, and a code comment records why.\n**Consequences:** Their runs still appear in the Actions tab, marked skipped. If the team ever publishes its own builds, the guard has to come off.\n\n### Decision 2: cutting backend PR time\n\n**Decision:** Refresh the build cache on every push to `main`, run the two unit-test passes as parallel jobs, and move Vitest coverage out of the `test-unit` → `sonarqube` chain. The time saving comes from the cache and from splitting the unit passes. Vitest moves so that a failing frontend test shows up in the first minutes of a run; today it runs inside `sonarqube`, which waits for both unit passes, about 25 minutes in.\n**Consequences:** One more job per backend PR. Each unit-test job sets up its own service containers. The 22-minute target is limited by the slowest database job, which is MySQL or MSSQL in most runs.\n\n### Decision 3: how the cache gets refreshed\n\n**Decision:** `cache-seeder` runs on every push to `main`. It saves under `gobuild-<go.sum hash>-<commit sha>` with a `restore-keys` fallback to the newest entry, and warms `-race -cover` as well as `-race`. Update the comment at `.github/actions/go-cache/action.yml:7-8` to give the new reason.\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- *Keep the key based only on `go.sum`.* A saved key can't be overwritten, so the cache never updates until `go.sum` changes.\n- *Let PR jobs save the cache.* A PR's cache is only visible to that PR and the PRs based on it, so other PRs can't use it, and several jobs writing at once would fight over the same key.\n**Rationale:** Caches saved from `main` are visible to every PR, and one key per commit means the newest build is always available.\n**Consequences:** Each entry is about 2.25 GB against the repo's 10 GB cache limit, so GitHub keeps about four and evicts the oldest. The `gomod` and `golint` caches share that limit, so eviction can drop them too and slow `lint-backend` and module downloads. One extra seeder run per merge.\n\n### Decision 4: running the suites on `main` and on demand\n\n**Decision:** Let the existing `pull-db-tests.yml` and `pull-e2e-tests.yml` jobs run on `push` to `main`, on `v*-csci435-*` tags and on `workflow_dispatch` (with a `ref` input that checkout uses), by changing each `pull_request`-only condition to `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || <the existing files-changed check>`. Pushes to `main` share one concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress` false, so a running job is never cancelled. Each tag and each manual run gets its own group, so it neither waits on nor replaces a `main` run. Pull request runs keep the group they have now.\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- *A new `main-suites.yml` that copies the jobs.* The copies would drift away from the PR jobs.\n- *Turn the jobs into one `workflow_call` workflow used by both.* No copies, but it rewrites upstream's files the most, which makes upstream syncs harder.\n- *Keep the `files-changed` filter on pushes to `main`, so docs-only merges skip the suites.* Most merges here are docs-only, and the two `db-tests` failures linked under Problem both came after docs-only merges, so repeat runs on an unchanged tree are how a flaky test shows up. Replacing the waiting run caps the cost at one queued run.\n**Rationale:** Changing the conditions keeps one definition for each job and touches as few upstream lines as possible. Starting a run by hand with a `ref` input works for old tags, which don't have this workflow file.\n**Consequences:** About 9 jobs per merge on `main`. When merges come in bursts, a waiting run is replaced by the newest one, so a failure may cover more than one merge, and the replaced run shows as cancelled on its commit; that saves runner time against the org's limit of 20 jobs. Every suite still `needs: files-changed`, so on push, tag and manual runs that job has to succeed (or be bypassed) even when it has no base to compare against, or every suite is skipped. A manual run takes the workflow file from `main` but `.github/actions/*` and the Makefile from the ref it checks out. `v1.27.3-csci435-s2` has the same actions and make targets as `main`; a ref from before those existed may not run.\n\n## Scope\n\nmedium, `scope: medium`. Changes `pull-db-tests.yml`, `pull-e2e-tests.yml`, `pull-compliance.yml` (timeouts), `cache-seeder.yml`, the `go-cache` action and the four release workflows. No product code changes. Evidence needs several pushes to `main`, a tag push, a manual run against a tag and four timed PR runs, each checked against the before numbers.\n\n---\n_Drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) for @controlled-opposition._","closedByPullRequestsReferences":[],"comments":[],"createdAt":"2026-11-14T02:04:40Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOTldkzc8AAAAC0JZx6A","name":"scope: medium","description":"","color":"1545a8"}],"milestone":{"number":4,"title":"Sprint 3","description":"","dueOn":"2026-11-19T00:00:00Z"},"number":181,"parent":null,"state":"OPEN","subIssues":{"nodes":[],"totalCount":0},"title":"Main's CI is red on every push and skips most test suites, and backend PRs wait about 28 minutes for checks","updatedAt":"2026-11-14T02:58:12Z","url":"https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/181"}

```text
## Issue format: hardening task

No GitHub template; write it in a blank issue. Used by hardening issues that don't fix a defect,
such as a flaky test or a broken CI check (Sprint 3, D2).

```markdown
## Problem
<What is unreliable now, and how you know: failing test names, run counts, CI run links.>
## Goal
<What "fixed" means.>
## Acceptance Criteria
----
### Hardening issues

Work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources: the
D8 baseline run (failing or flaky tests, broken CI checks on `main`); the "Introduced" and
"Encountered" Tech Debt fields of Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs; bugs found in reviews or after
merging; and the upstream issue tracker for the parts of Gitea the team works on. It is scoped like
any other issue and must include evidence that the problem is fixed:

| Kind | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Bug fix | A test that fails before the fix and passes after |
| Flaky test | The root cause, and repeated runs before and after the fix (e.g. 20 for a unit test, 10 for E2E) |
| Broken or missing CI check | Links to CI runs before and after the fix |
| Failing tests in the baseline | Pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group of failures |

The site doesn't say where the evidence goes: plan it in the issue (Evidence of Fix, or Additional
Information for a bug), then post the results on the issue and in the PR's Test Evidence once the
fix is in. Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause
counts as small at most.

### Design Decision and spec review
```

=== go-cache action
name: go-caches
description: Restore the go module, build, and golangci-lint caches. Save only on the cache-seeder workflow.

# Only the cache-seeder workflow saves; rename requires updating cache-seeder.yml.
# The lint job restores but does not save the gobuild cache, so only one writer
# (the gobuild job) populates it and there is no contention on the cache key.
# Seeder restores by exact key only (no restore-keys) so each go.sum seeds a clean
# cache and size stays bounded; do not add restore-keys here. PR runs keep them.

inputs:
  lint-cache:
    description: Restore (and save in cache-seeder) ~/.cache/golangci-lint
    default: "false"

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - if: ${{ github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' }}
      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ~/go/pkg/mod
        key: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    - if: ${{ github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' }}
      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ~/go/pkg/mod
        key: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
        restore-keys: gomod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
    - if: ${{ github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' && inputs.lint-cache != 'true' }}
      uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/go-build
        key: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    - if: ${{ github.workflow != 'cache-seeder' || inputs.lint-cache == 'true' }}
      uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/go-build
        key: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
        restore-keys: gobuild-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
    - if: ${{ inputs.lint-cache == 'true' && github.workflow == 'cache-seeder' }}

# Populates main's cache scope so PR runs warm-start from it. Saves the go
# module, go build (incl. test compile), and golangci-lint caches.
#
# Caches are ref-scoped: PR runs read their own scope then fall back to the
# base branch. Per .github/actions/go-cache/action.yml, PRs are restore-only,
# so push-to-main is the only opportunity to populate the fallback scope.

name: cache-seeder

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - "go.sum"
      - ".golangci.yml"
      - ".github/actions/go-cache/action.yml"
      - ".github/actions/go-setup/action.yml"
      - ".github/workflows/cache-seeder.yml"

concurrency:
  group: cache-seeder
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  gobuild:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/go-setup
      - run: make deps-backend deps-tools

name: db-tests

on:
  pull_request:
  push: # on main the database jobs are skipped; test-unit and sonarqube run so SonarQube has a main branch to compare pull requests with
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  files-changed:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/files-changed.yml

  test-pgsql-shard-1:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.files-changed.outputs.backend == 'true'
    needs: files-changed
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  test-unit:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || needs.files-changed.outputs.backend == 'true' # main always gets Go coverage
    needs: files-changed
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      elasticsearch:
        image: docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.19.15
        env:
          discovery.type: single-node
          xpack.security.enabled: false
          xpack.ml.enabled: false
          ingest.geoip.downloader.enabled: false
          ES_JAVA_OPTS: "-Xms1g -Xmx1g"
        ports:
          - "9200:9200"
      meilisearch:
        image: getmeili/meilisearch:v1
        env:
          MEILI_ENV: development # disable auth
        ports:
          - "7700:7700"
      redis:
        image: redis:latest@sha256:c904002d182255b6db3cbe3a1e8ce6c187d15390c39500b59fc07181aabff7bf
        options: >- # wait until redis has started
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
      minio:
        image: bitnamilegacy/minio:2025.7.23
        env:
          MINIO_ROOT_USER: 123456
          MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: 12345678
        ports:
          - "9000:9000"
      devstoreaccount1.azurite.local: # https://github.com/Azure/Azurite/issues/1583
        image: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-storage/azurite:latest@sha256:dae2a5f96553962901304b94e72ef87e299d0825e4b679673bcc527a25076fe4
        ports:
          - 10000:10000
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/go-setup
      - name: Add hosts to /etc/hosts
        run: '[ -e "/.dockerenv" ] || [ -e "/run/.containerenv" ] || echo "127.0.0.1 minio devstoreaccount1.azurite.local mysql elasticsearch meilisearch smtpimap" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts'
      - run: make deps-backend
      - run: make generate-go
        env:
          TAGS: bindata
      - name: unit-tests
        run: make test-backend
        env:
          GOTEST_FLAGS: -race -timeout=20m -coverprofile=coverage.out
          TAGS: bindata
          GITHUB_READ_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_READ_TOKEN }}
      - name: coverage-paths
        run: sed -i 's|^gitea\.dev/||' coverage.out # SonarQube expects paths relative to the repository, not module paths
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: go-coverage
          path: coverage.out
          retention-days: 1
      - name: unit-tests-gogit
        run: make test-backend
        env:
          GOTEST_FLAGS: -race -timeout=20m
          TAGS: bindata gogit
          GOEXPERIMENT:
          GITHUB_READ_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_READ_TOKEN }}
          GITEA_TEST_CI_SKIP_EXTERNAL: true
      - run: make test-check

  sonarqube:
    # runs when test-unit was skipped too, so every pull request gets a scan (without Go coverage then)
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) }} # forks get no SONAR_TOKEN
    needs: test-unit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # SonarQube tells new code from old by the git history
      - uses: ./.github/actions/node-setup
      - run: make deps-frontend
      - name: frontend-coverage
        run: pnpm exec vitest run --coverage.enabled --coverage.provider=v8 --coverage.reporter=lcovonly --coverage.include='web_src/js/**' --coverage.include='tools/eslint-rules/**' # where vitest.config.ts finds tests
      - if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.test-unit.result != 'skipped' }} # a failed step here or later in test-unit must not drop the Go coverage
        continue-on-error: true # no artifact when test-unit's first test run failed; then the scan has no Go coverage
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: go-coverage
      - if: ${{ !cancelled() }} # scan even when the frontend tests failed, without their coverage
        uses: SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@d209202bc7d53ff1cc128f7f907dac145c9d6ae9 # v8.3.0
        env:
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}

  least 2 medium and 1 small. Either load can be met with equivalent story points instead. Every
  issue has exactly **one** assignee. Unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into the backlog before new

  find areas that still need work (features, improvements, test gaps, bugs) and write new issues

  tells the team. Split it into sub-issues, each with one owner, its own spec (D2) and scope, linked
  to the feature issue and added to the `Sprint 3` milestone. Sub-issues count toward the load.
- **D2:** specs are written and spec-reviewed before coding starts. Features use the user story
  format; hardening issues use the bug report format when they fix a defect, otherwise the

  keeps it in the issue body. Decisions that span issues go in `docs/sprint3/design.md`.
